scope: Paper proof only: research/prime_field_ic_closure_20261112/finish/lifting/PROOF.md, checked line by line by one adversarial checker ('sound with gaps'; reading in research/notes/index-calculus/PRIME_FIELD_IC_CLOSURE_20261112.md section 5). Petsche checked against arXiv math/0508160v2; Silverman 1990 Thm 1.1 recalled from memory (constants may change, the asymptotics not). Not covered: r growing with p; Silverman-Suzuki/Miller hybrids that use other rational points of E' (open); Q-curve and number-field lifts (Prop 3 is a sketch); non-homomorphic p-adic sections; concrete sizes (r >= 7 not excluded at 256 bits, r >= 6 under worst-case rho_G). The toy xedni (8-16 bits, 69,425 honest trials) illustrates and proves nothing. research-kb prior-art check not done.
statement: Lifting attacks on prime-field ECDLP (xedni/JKSST type, A8), Theorem 2: any lifting procedure that draws fresh uniform masks per trial (every mask draw counted as a trial, rejected or aborted ones included), outputs lifts over Q of at most beta bits and uses relations only among the r sampled lifted points has per-trial success probability at most O_r(beta^{3r(r-1)} log^{r(r-1)} beta)/q. For fixed r, polynomial-size lifts and log log p = o(log q), the expected number of trials is at least q/(log p)^{O(r^2)} = q^{1-o(1)}, above Pollard rho's sqrt(q). The proof assumes no conjecture: Petsche 2006 Thm 2 with the Szpiro-ratio bound over Q replaces Lang's conjecture, with Silverman 1990 and Mazur's torsion bound. The per-mask bound does not depend on the lift.
